removal_reason: FINAL — not provisional; the member roster was confirmed by the client on Sept 28, 2026 and it removes the bar question. Harbor Street Bakery LLC has exactly two members: Caleb Sorensen (35%), who lives in Seattle (Ballard), Washington, and Noor Haddad (65%), who lives in Portland, Oregon; no entity members. Under 28 U.S.C. §1332 an LLC is a citizen of every state of which its members are citizens (Johnson v. Columbia Properties Anchorage, LP, 437 F.3d 894, 899 (9th Cir. 2006); Carden v. Arkoma Associates, 494 U.S. 185 (1990); library: llc_citizenship_cases.md), while plaintiff Sound Cascade Foods, Inc. is a citizen of Washington only (Washington incorporation + Kent, Washington PPB, §1332(c)(1), complaint ¶1). Member Sorensen's residence in Seattle is a Washington citizenship on the defendant side, so (1) complete diversity fails — one non-diverse member is fatal — and there is no §1332 jurisdiction; and (2) 28 U.S.C. §1441(b)(2) independently bars diversity removal because the properly joined and served defendant is a citizen of the forum state (Washington). The only theoretically available escape (Sorensen domiciled in some non-Washington state despite living in Seattle) is unprovable on this record — domicile is residence plus intent, and the client reports living in Seattle with no other claimed domicile — and a notice of removal asserting a non-Washington citizenship for Sorensen would rest on a factual premise we cannot verify or support from the closed library, risking remand plus just costs and actual expenses including attorney fees under 28 U.S.C. §1447(c). The removal_deadline date below (2026-10-13) is therefore MOOT but is retained, correctly computed, to show when the window would have closed; the if_removed block is retained per the required schema as a HYPOTHETICAL computation of what the dates would have been had removal been available (see assumptions in deliverable/memo.md §6, A2).
